key_insight: The paper combines interpretable linear meta-learning with adaptive uncertainty calibration to make multi-objective molecular search faster, more transferable, and more effective than standard surrogates.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, low-compute active-learning framework for chemistry optimization where multiple competing objectives and limited data make deep models hard to deploy.
method: Meta-train linear surrogate models across chemical objectives and cheap auxiliary properties to transfer knowledge to new targets.
Embed the surrogate in an Efficient Global Optimization (EGO) loop for multi-objective discovery.
Use adaptive confidence tuning to recalibrate uncertainty and balance exploration vs. exploitation during search.
evidence_signal: On a large-scale real search for spin-crossover metal-organic complexes, the baseline was 78% worse in Pareto performance, and dynamic confidence tuning beat over 50% of the statically calibrated front.
watch_item: The approach depends on good calibration and transfer across related objectives, so performance may drop if the auxiliary tasks are poorly matched or the uncertainty model is miscalibrated.
paper_title: Interpretable Meta-Learning for Multi-Objective Chemical Search
